title: Curvefield — Elliptic-Curve Cryptography Lab
description: An interactive ECC lab: the geometric group law, finite-field curves, a from-scratch secp256k1 cryptosystem (ECDSA + BIP-340 Schnorr + MuSig2), Curve25519, and a hand-written BLS12-381 pairing — now standards-grade and the substrate for a from-scratch Groth16 zk-SNARK. RFC 9380 hash-to-curve (expand_message_xmd, Simplified SWU with the 11-/3-isogenies, cofactor clearing) reproduces the RFC's own G1/G2 test vectors; ZCash/Ethereum point serialization, IRTF BLS signatures with HKDF KeyGen (matching the EIP-2333 vector) and proof-of-possession, and an optimized Hayashida–Aranha final exponentiation round out a production-shaped pairing stack. The Groth16 lab proves knowledge of a secret (x³+x+5=out) in three group elements, verified by one pairing equation, and a from-scratch PLONK lab proves the *same* statement with a universal setup — selector-gate arithmetization, a copy-constraint permutation argument, a grand-product polynomial, and a transparent KZG-batched verifier — so the two SNARKs sit side by side. From-scratch BULLETPROOFS add a Fiat–Shamir inner-product argument that folds the witness in half each round, giving aggregated logarithmic range proofs (a 64-bit amount in ~16 group elements, ~20× smaller than the linear form) checked by both a transparent and an optimized single-multiexp verifier, plus a full confidential transaction — homomorphic kernel-excess balance over an aggregated range proof, the Monero/Mimblewimble structure, with an inflation attack shown to break it. Plus Schnorr adaptor signatures and atomic swaps, BIP-32 HD wallets, Shamir/Feldman secret sharing, FROST threshold signatures, zero-knowledge Σ-protocols (Pedersen, Chaum–Pedersen, range proofs), KZG polynomial commitments, and discrete-log + invalid-curve attacks. A from-scratch STARK rounds out the proof-system shelf: the one system here that needs no elliptic curve and no trusted setup — transparent and plausibly post-quantum, resting on a hash alone. It proves an actual execution (a Fibonacci-square recurrence) over the Goldilocks field p = 2⁶⁴ − 2³² + 1 with a hand-written NTT, Merkle commitments, a Fiat–Shamir transcript, DEEP out-of-domain sampling, and a full FRI low-degree test — and demonstrates soundness live by rejecting a forged intermediate step. A VERIFIABLE RANDOM FUNCTION lab implements ECVRF (RFC 9381) on Edwards25519 in both ciphersuites — try-and-increment and the constant-time Elligator2 map — reproducing the RFC's own proof (π) test vectors byte-for-byte and driving a verifiable leader-election lottery. A LINKABLE RING SIGNATURE lab builds Monero's anonymity core from scratch — SAG, bLSAG, and the concise CLSAG with key images I = x·Hₚ(P), plus CryptoNote stealth one-time addresses — assembled into a complete private payment that hides the sender yet still catches a double-spend. A SEALED secure-channel lab closes the one missing dimension — confidentiality — by assembling the whole engine into the SIGNAL PROTOCOL, the end-to-end encryption behind WhatsApp and Signal: a from-scratch ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (RFC 8439, pinned byte-for-byte), HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869), XEdDSA prekey signatures, X3DH key agreement with an offline recipient, and the Double Ratchet that gives every message forward secrecy and heals the session one round trip after a full key compromise — driven by a live Alice⇄Bob chat you can tamper with, reorder, and compromise. A POST-QUANTUM lattice lab adds ML-KEM (FIPS 203, the standardised CRYSTALS-Kyber) built entirely from scratch — a hand-written Keccak/SHA-3 + SHAKE sponge (pinned to the FIPS 202 digests), the negacyclic number-theoretic transform over Z₃₃₂₉[X]/(X²⁵⁶+1) with a base multiply pinned to a schoolbook convolution, centered-binomial noise, Compress/Decompress ciphertext coding, and the Fujisaki–Okamoto transform with implicit rejection — for all three parameter sets (ML-KEM-512/768/1024), matching the standard's key and ciphertext byte-sizes exactly and demonstrating IND-CCA2 by catching a mauled ciphertext; wired into the real TLS 1.3 X25519MLKEM768 hybrid handshake so a classical curve and a lattice KEM secure one session together. A SECURE-COMPUTATION lab opens a whole new pillar — computing on inputs two parties never share — with Yao's two-party protocol built from scratch: a Chou–Orlandi oblivious transfer on this lab's Ed25519 group (the sender never learns the receiver's choice; the receiver opens only one message), then garbled circuits with the free-XOR and half-gate optimizations (XOR and NOT are free; an AND costs the proven-minimal two ciphertexts) over 128-bit labels from the lab's own SHA-256. It runs Yao's original Millionaires' Problem — who is richer, revealing nothing else — plus private equality, sum, and product, each with an auditable transcript and a live single-byte-tamper integrity demo, verified exhaustively against a plaintext oracle over every 4-bit input pair. All computed live in the browser, pinned to published test vectors, with zero crypto dependencies.
